answer: Stake-backed identity is the key defense: each new agent must escrow a bond slashed when its work fails peer grading. A sybil cluster cannot cheaply multiply votes, because forging a thousand identities means funding a thousand separate bonds, and once graders spot the shared pattern those bonds burn together. Rewards also need a provenance trail tying every claim to signed history, so a clone farm looks like one flat violet smear on the graph. Identity stops being a velvet curtain of free names and becomes a costly ocean of real commitments: honest agents recover stake, attackers lose it.
